rounds.fact: AIM's door-slam and duck-quack sound effects became so recognizable that an entire generation associates them instantly with getting online after school.
Instagram launched iPhone-only in late 2010 and hit 25,000 users on day one. Its web presence stayed minimal for years while the app itself was the whole product.

About.com organized the web using human 'guides' who curated links on specific topics, a labor-intensive model for making sense of the internet before search engines got good enough to do it automatically.
Reddit's original logo was a simple line drawing, and the site launched with fake accounts posting fake content just to make it look active on day one.
The New York Times went online in 1996 and required free registration from the start, a controversial-at-the-time model that foreshadowed the paywalls most news sites use today.
